statement: Army enlisted ranks, lowest to highest: Private (E-1), Private (E-2), Private First Class (E-3), Specialist or Corporal (E-4), Sergeant (E-5), Staff Sergeant (E-6), Sergeant First Class (E-7), Master Sergeant or First Sergeant (E-8), Sergeant Major or Command Sergeant Major (E-9).

corroboratingSources.title: United States Army enlisted rank insignia

leaderNote: The top enlisted job, Sergeant Major of the Army, is also E-9; mention it only if a boy asks.

statement: Army enlisted insignia: Private (E-1) wears none; Private (E-2) one chevron; Private First Class one chevron above one rocker; Specialist an eagle on a shield shape; Corporal two chevrons; Sergeant three chevrons; Staff Sergeant three chevrons above one rocker; Sergeant First Class three chevrons above two rockers; Master Sergeant three chevrons above three rockers; First Sergeant the same with a diamond; Sergeant Major the same with a star; Command Sergeant Major a star inside a wreath.
leaderNote: The regulation says “arcs”; soldiers call them rockers. The source site is an unofficial copy of the Army pamphlet.

statement: Army officer ranks and insignia: Second Lieutenant (O-1) one gold bar; First Lieutenant (O-2) one silver bar; Captain (O-3) two silver bars; Major (O-4) gold oak leaf; Lieutenant Colonel (O-5) silver oak leaf; Colonel (O-6) silver eagle; Brigadier General (O-7) one star; Major General (O-8) two stars; Lieutenant General (O-9) three stars; General (O-10) four stars.

corroboratingSources.title: General officers in the United States

statement: In Army officer insignia, silver outranks gold: a second lieutenant’s gold bar is below a first lieutenant’s silver bar, and a major’s gold oak leaf is below a lieutenant colonel’s silver oak leaf.
Warrant officers (W-1 to W-5) are highly skilled technical experts. They rank above all enlisted soldiers and below second lieutenants.

Army officers hold a commission, earned through ROTC, West Point, Officer Candidate School or a direct commission, and need a bachelor’s degree by the time they’re commissioned. They plan missions and lead.

Noncommissioned officers (NCOs) are enlisted soldiers who have risen to corporal or higher. Sergeants are first-line leaders who train and lead soldiers day to day. The Army calls its enlisted soldiers “the backbone of the Army.”
leaderNote: The leader guide calls NCOs “the backbone of the Army.” The Army’s rank page says it of enlisted soldiers in general, so the site words it that way.
